page: Microsoft Azure D2pls_v7 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs and 4.0 GB of memory, resulting in an allocation of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Built on the arm64 architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance provides dedicated compute cores without hardware hyper-threading or specialized x86 vector extensions.

The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware accelerators, operating without attached GPUs. It is designated as Premium Storage capable, requiring network-attached remote block volumes for persistent disk storage, operating system disks, and application data workloads. Complimentary public IPv4 addresses are not included.

With a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the D2pls_v7 trades large memory allocations for compute density. This profile provides architectural cost efficiency for workloads that require dedicated processing threads without high RAM capacity. Suitable deployment targets include containerized microservices, light web servers, network gateways, build workers, and ARM-native software test environments.
description: Microsoft Azure D2pls_v7 is an ARM-based general-purpose instance providing 2 dedicated vCPUs and 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. Executing on the arm64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance does not include integrated GPUs or local scratch storage, relying instead on network-attached remote block storage through its Premium Storage capability. The reduced memory footprint delivers cost-effective dedicated compute capacity for applications that do not demand extensive RAM pools. Lacking hardware acceleration and local disk, it is optimized for lightweight compute tasks, containerized microservices, build pipelines, front-end web serving, and ARM-specific compilation environments.
